Add file lock mechanism Some systems, such as Android, do not support SysV semaphore locks. This implements an alternative file lock mechanism using flock(). flock() was chosen because it's pretty straight forward. It's known to be broken when using NFS, but I doubt we'll ever store our lock on an NFS volume. For now the SysV semaphore lock is still in the codebase. It's arguably better than the file lock and mosys was designed to be flexible beyond the needs of ChromeOS, though in reality the SysV semaphore lock probably won't be used anymore. stressapptest: Add flag for use free memory only or total memory For the case of tests using stressapptest for "memory validation", it should test give ratio according to system total memory (and abort if the condition can't meet). However for devices on run-in rack, they may be running multiple stress tests in parallel - for example stressapptest (for CPU & RAM), glbench (for GPU), and other tests for network or audio. And we can't expect how much memory will be free at that time - so using the ration for "free memory" would be the better idea. This change adds a new argument to specify should we use only free memory or not (i.e., total memory). BUG=None TEST=Run stressapptest on Lucid. fixture test list: scan serial number support Station-based fixtures need to be able to keep track of the serial number of the current device being tested, which should then be stored into DeviceData on the Goofy device. This adds support in the fixture test list to clear DeviceData when the fixture_entry test is run, and also (by default) turns the fixture-based test list into an AutomatedSequence, so the serial numbers are always properly cleared before and after the test list's sequence of tests are run. Also add support to "press spacebar" before running the sequence of tests (useful for cases when the operator still has to perform some task before starting the station, e.g. closing an RF chamber). build_time_stats: Add build success ratio to reports. Adjust BuildTimings to have a success flag, and populate all stats on all builds before producing the reports. Generally, pass all build_timings around, instead of only the successful ones so that pass/fail values can be calculated as needed. We still only use successful builds to calculate stage timing stats, since failed builds would distort the results.
